issues.title: Missing positivity condition for strict monotonicity
issues.failure_explanation: The proof cites S'>0 and P'>0 but omits the multiplier h-delta^mu in shapfunc0. If delta^mu=h, phi is constant on every I^j; if delta^mu>h, it decreases there and the stated bounds2 even has a negative right-hand side for an absolute value. Hence the lemma's strict-increase claim is false under its stated hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: Shape-Lemma0 and the strict-increase and derivative-nonvanishing assertions in Inner-Lemma fail for parameter values expressly allowed by the old source, including the equality used in its numerical setup.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose the standing condition 0<δ^μ<h in Shape-Lemma0 and every downstream invocation, replace h≥δ^μ by h>δ^μ in Inner-Lemma, and change or rerun numerical examples that used equality. Then on each I^j the derivative contains the positive factor (h−δ^μ)/(h−δ), restoring strict increase, the stated derivative-zero set, and the bounds without changing the construction or convergence guarantees.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine invalid inference by omitting the multiplier h−δ^μ, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, strict positivity is a short, routine qualification on an auxiliary tuning parameter; choosing a nearby nondegenerate value preserves the same strict-monotonicity statement, method, and rates.

issues.title: Invalid unit normalization on a nonintegral grid

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We also introduce a new parameter $J=\lceil\frac 1 {N\delta}\rceil=\lceil\frac 1 h \rceil,$

issues.failure_explanation: PsiqxAS asserts phi(1+(1-q)delta)-phi((1-q)delta)=1 under the preceding assumptions h=Ndelta and J=ceil(1/h). The block construction gives only h-shift equivariance, so a unit shift has this value uniformly when 1/h is integral, not for general h. For example, N=5, delta=0.036, h=0.18, mu=1 and q=1 are allowed, but shapfunc0 gives phi(1)=0.936+0.144P(4/9), approximately 0.9931, while phi(0)=0. Thus the cancelled denominator is not one.
issues.overall_effect: The unnormalized inner-function formula, its derivative estimates, the mapped-center formulas and separation bounds are not valid for the stated general grid. MainResult also incorrectly identifies h^alpha with J^{-alpha} when J=ceil(1/h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt the integral-grid convention already used in the constructive algorithm: choose J∈N, set h=1/J and δ=1/(NJ), and remove J=ceil(1/h) as the general definition. Iterating φ(t+h)=φ(t)+h then gives φ(t+1)=φ(t)+1, so the normalization denominator is exactly one and the inner, center, separation, and derivative formulas retain their stated form. For the refinement claim, choose J=ceil(N^(1+γ)) and then set h=1/J and δ=1/(NJ), which preserves the advertised asymptotic rate.
issues.why_classification: The unit-shift cancellation is a substantive false inference, not a transcriptional error. Its complete repair is nevertheless the local, source-supported restriction to a reciprocal integral grid; h and δ are design parameters, and this restriction changes neither the method, target class, conclusion, nor asymptotic rate.

issues.title: Rational independence is insufficient for center separation
issues.failure_explanation: For q=1 and d=2, take an integral grid with J>=3 and choose delta^mu=h/sqrt(2). Then the first two interior univariate center values are C=(h+delta^mu)/2 and C+h. Set lambda_1/lambda_2=(C+h)/C=5-2sqrt(2) and normalize their sum to one. The ratio is irrational, so lambda_1 and lambda_2 are rationally independent, yet the mapped centers with indices (0,-1) and (-1,1) satisfy lambda_1 C=lambda_2(C+h). Thus Cor:Dist is false. Its proof's assertion that the relevant coefficients are rational is not established under the old hypotheses, and its additional cross-level claim also fails at shared endpoint centers.
issues.overall_effect: The rationally independent branch of the construction has no guaranteed collision-free center encoding; one scalar abscissa can carry different sampled values, so MainResult cannot rely on that branch as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the rationally independent branch by the finite nonresonance condition that, for each fixed q and any two distinct geometric centers, Σ_p λ_p[ψ_q(c_q^{j_p})−ψ_q(c_q^{j'_p})]≠0. Carry this condition into MainResult and state Cor:Dist level by level; cross-level coincidences at shared endpoint centers should be permitted because different q have different outer functions and the shared centers carry the same sample. The exceptional choices form a finite union of proper hyperplanes in the positive λ-simplex for each grid, so admissible normalized rationally independent choices remain generic and can be selected after checking the finite center set.
issues.why_classification: Rational independence over the rationals does not justify the old proof, so the issue is not a typo. The additional finite nonresonance condition is a routine technical nondegeneracy qualification excluding exceptional resonant parameters; it preserves the center-encoding method, Hölder conclusion, rate, and intended regular parameter regime without a new proof architecture.

issues.title: Row-dependent interpolation does not define a global outer function
issues.failure_explanation: Definition Defn:Outer constructs functions indexed by rows, but the later assignment identifies g_q at an input through a row-dependent g_q^{i_l}. The old source expressly permits consecutive mapped rows to interlace. For example, in two dimensions with an allowed near-balanced rationally independent lambda and f(x_1,x_2)=x_2, each interpolant along an x_1-row is the distinct constant c_q^{j_2}/N, while the scalar domains of adjacent rows overlap. The same t can therefore receive different values from two preimages, so no single C^2 univariate g_q has been constructed.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed outer functions and hence the Kolmogorov superposition f_N are not well-defined in the asserted form for the full old parameter class, leaving MainResult without its required construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the row-selected assignment by a genuinely global construction. Restrict to a strictly center-separated hierarchical choice of λ, such as one satisfying the old λPQ inequalities with margin, and choose r=δ^μ<h sufficiently close to h. At r=h the finite row-major center set has a positive minimum scalar gap; continuity together with diam(Ψ_q(C_q^j))≤|λ|_1(h−r) shows that, for r<h sufficiently close to h, the complete scalar image intervals of all hypercubes remain ordered and pairwise disjoint. Define one g_q to equal f(c_q^j)/N on each such image interval and join consecutive plateaus with the shape function S, extending constantly at the endpoints. This gives a single C^2 univariate outer function and makes g_q∘Ψ_q independent of any row or preimage choice; the unrestricted rationally independent branch must be removed unless comparable full-image separation is proved.
issues.why_classification: Merely relabeling the row interpolants cannot resolve overlapping domains with conflicting values. A complete repair needs a new full-image separation argument, a restricted parameter choice, and a replacement global gluing construction, so it exceeds a minor local correction. The perturbative separation route is nevertheless contained within the outer-function construction and preserves arbitrary Hölder targets, strict C^2 inner functions, the number of summands, and the approximation mechanism, so neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is necessary.

issues.title: Invalid geometric estimate for gap levels
issues.failure_explanation: MainResult claims an O(h^alpha) contribution at every level. For a gap level, however, choosebox minimizes scalar image distance |Psi_q(x)-a_q^j|, which does not control ||x-c_q^j||_2. Thus Oscf3's bound by sqrt(d)h/2 is unjustified and can fail under the dislocations already described in the old source. The new proof allows distance sqrt(d), counts at most d gap levels, and obtains an O(N^{-1}) gap term.
issues.overall_effect: The old h^alpha estimate and the advertised O(N^{-alpha(1+gamma)}) refinement rate are not established. A gap contribution of order N^{-1} remains regardless of further refinement in J.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Oscf3 by the only generally valid bounds for a gap level and use that at most d levels are gaps. This yields a corrected estimate of the form ||f−f_N||_∞≤c_α(1+d^(α/2)/2^α)h^α+2c_αd^(α/2+1)/N. Consequently, when J is of order N^(1+γ), the rate is O(N^(−α(1+γ))+N^(−1)), not a pure O(N^(−α(1+γ))); the refinement statement and abstract must be changed accordingly. In particular, the canonical choice J=N still gives O(N^(−α)).
issues.why_classification: The correction is a contained change to the geometric estimate and error summation, with no new construction or global proof architecture. It is not minor because it introduces an N^(−1) floor and withdraws the advertised unrestricted refinement rate. The resulting Hölder approximation theorem and its standard O(N^(−α)) regime remain recognizably comparable, so the loss is limited rather than major.

issues.title: Singular high-dimensional numerical target
issues.failure_explanation: In eg2D3D4D, choose x_2=1, x_3=pi/2-1 and the remaining x_p=0. These coordinates lie in [0,1] when d>=3, but tan(x_2+...+x_d) is undefined. For x_1>0, exp(x_1 tan(s)) tends to infinity from one side of the pole and to zero from the other, so the expression has no continuous extension. It therefore cannot supply the intended continuous Hölder test on the stated cube.
issues.overall_effect: The reported d=3,4,9 experiment does not use a well-defined continuous target in the class covered by MainResult, so it cannot serve as the claimed high-dimensional convergence verification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the singular factor exp(x_1 tan(x_2+⋯+x_d)) by a concrete smooth bounded alternative on the cube, for example exp(x_1 cos(x_2+⋯+x_d)), verify that the resulting u and the zero-extended u log|u| have the claimed continuity/Hölder regularity, and rerun all d≥3 experiments and regenerate their plots and reported errors. The old numerical data cannot be retained as verification unless they are independently shown to have used the corrected target.
issues.why_classification: No correction is uniquely forced by the old formula, so this is not a typo. It is confined to an illustrative numerical target and has no formal dependents; replacing it by a comparable smooth test and rerunning the experiments is a routine local repair requiring no new mathematical argument or loss of a theorem.
